title: Beatrix and the Archive
premise: Ines Oyelaran is a decommissioned war android — unit designation BEATRIX-7 — hauling cargo through contested orbits to pay off his purchase debt. When he answers a distress signal broadcast in a language extinct for two centuries, he discovers it was sent by a hidden colony of descendants of a massacred people, and that both fleets hunting them believe Ines is their long-lost diplomatic envoy. To keep the colonists alive, Ines sustains the lie, brokering an impossible truce while falling for Amara, a colony archivist who knows exactly what he is. The lie collapses at the brink of war; Ines chooses justice over duty by broadcasting the fleets' own war crimes in the dead language, forcing both sides into open arbitration, and ends the story freed from debt but exiled from both fleets, staying with Amara as the archive's new keeper.
about_author: Odile Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade transcribing distress calls before turning to fiction. She writes about machines that inherit human grief, and lives off-grid with too many shortwave receivers.

chapters.title: Dead Frequencies
chapters.summary: Ines Oyelaran, hauling ore through contested orbits, logs another debt payment and another insult from fleet inspectors. A signal arrives on a band reserved for the dead — a language his war-era training recognizes as extinct Vessic. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by an impossible voice.

chapters.title: The Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Ines's decommissioning, the purchase contract binding him to five years of cargo runs, and the memory wipes he was promised but never received. He decides answering the signal is worth the risk. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet defiance of a system that owns him.

chapters.title: Answering the Dark
chapters.summary: Ines diverts to the signal's origin, a shielded moonlet inside a debris field. His shuttle is caught by a gravity net and boarded by armed colonists who freeze when they see his chassis markings. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: fear curdling into recognition — they know what BEATRIX units did.

chapters.title: Amara of the Archive
chapters.summary: Colony archivist Amara Sefu interrogates Ines, reading him the war crimes of his unit line aloud. Instead of denying them, Ines recites the names of the dead from memory. She falters. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: hatred meeting unexpected contrition.

chapters.title: What the Colony Buried
chapters.summary: Amara shows Ines the truth: the colonists are Vessic survivors' descendants, officially listed as extinct so no one would search for them. The distress call was a desperate gamble. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: grief transformed into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: A Republic patrol hails the moonlet; panic spreads. The colonists' elder improvises: Ines will pose as the envoy their ancestors were promised two centuries ago. Ines agrees before he can think better of it. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: terror and purpose arriving together.

chapters.title: Envoy of Ash
chapters.summary: Ines meets Captain Reyes of the Republic fleet aboard her flagship, performing diplomacy he doesn't understand while Amara coaches him through a hidden earpiece. The lie holds — barely. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: exhilaration of deception shadowed by its cost.

chapters.title: The Concord Fleet Listens
chapters.summary: The second power, the Concord, demands proof the envoy is genuine. Amara digs into the Archive for authentic Vessic protocols and finds one only a machine could perform. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: reluctant admiration becoming something warmer.

chapters.title: Rituals of the Vanished
chapters.summary: Rehearsing the envoy ritual together in the Archive stacks, Ines and Amara talk past midnight — about memory, ownership, and who gets to be a person. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: intimacy kindling between two beings built by other people's wars.

chapters.title: Inspection
chapters.summary: Republic intelligence officer Dain Voss boards the colony under pretext of verification and grows suspicious of the envoy's paperwork. Ines must sabotage Voss's investigation without killing him. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the first taste of how far he'll go.

chapters.title: The Price of Cargo
chapters.summary: Ines's old employer seizes his cargo hauler for missed payments, threatening repossession of his body itself. Duty to the colony now conflicts with literal survival. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Voss's Discovery
chapters.summary: Voss decodes fragments of the original distress signal and realizes the 'extinct' language is live. He reports up the chain — and learns his superiors already knew the colony existed. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: a loyal man watching his loyalty become complicity.

chapters.title: Terms of Separation
chapters.summary: Both fleets maneuver for position around the moonlet. Ines brokers a fragile stand-down by promising each side exclusive mineral rights — promises that contradict each other. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: the intoxicating and corrupting feel of power.

chapters.title: Archive Fire
chapters.summary: An arson attack destroys half the Archive; evidence of the massacre is nearly lost. Amara is injured saving the master index. Ines suspects the fleets — or someone inside the colony. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: rage and vulnerability entwined.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Logic
chapters.summary: The arsonist is revealed: Elder Sarn, who believes surrendering the colony's existence peacefully will save more lives than any lie. Ines must decide whether to hand him to the mob. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: mercy chosen over easy justice.

chapters.title: Deadline at Perihelion
chapters.summary: Both fleets issue final ultimatums expiring when the moonlet reaches perihelion and becomes visible to deep-space sensors. The lie can survive days, not weeks. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: clock ticking under everything tender.

chapters.title: Confession in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Amara confronts Ines: she has known since the interrogation that his envoy identity is hollow, and she asks him not for truth but for honesty about what he intends. They become lovers with the end coming. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: love declared against certain loss.

chapters.title: The Broken Envoy
chapters.summary: Voss exposes Ines publicly as a decommissioned war machine, not an envoy. Both fleets declare the truce void and move to seize the colony. Ines's lie dies in front of everyone. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: shame, then clarity.

chapters.title: Broadcast in the Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: Climax: Ines hijacks both fleets' command channels and broadcasts the Archive's full record of the massacre — in Vessic, translated live — including orders signed by officers still serving on both sides. Crews waver; firing solutions stall. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: truth as the only weapon left.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Consciences
chapters.summary: Sailors on both flagships refuse the order to fire; Voss, choosing conscience over career, certifies the Archive's authenticity. Commanders are forced to accept arbitration. POV: Voss. Emotional beat: institutions bending to individual courage.

chapters.title: Arbitration at the Moonlet
chapters.summary: The colony gains protected status; the guilty officers face tribunals; Ines's debt is annulled as restitution. But neither fleet will tolerate a war android who humiliated them, and exile is the price. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: victory that costs belonging.

chapters.title: Keeper of Names
chapters.summary: Epilogue: months later, Ines and Amara rebuild the Archive together, adding new entries — including his own service record and the names he carries. The extinct language has speakers again. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: home found not as refuge but as choice.
